pages.text: Mom went to market, leaving the yard empty. "Today I will do all the farm work." Pipo puffed out his chest.
Morning work meant letting sheep onto the hill. Pipo opened the pen gate gently.
The three grown-ups rushed over. "You cannot do it alone! We will help!"
Grandpa tapped his stick in the old way. Sheep rushed this way, then that way.
Mr. Horse ran with a mountain of hay. Beside him, Mrs. Goose chattered without stopping.
Crash! Whoosh! All three fell, tangled together in the hay. Only legs kicked outside the pile.
"We... need a little rest." They flopped down on the hay.
Alone, Pipo steadily filled the water tub. Baskets of eggs already stood neatly in the yard.
As the sun sank, the last sheep slipped into the pen. Pipo gently shut the gate.
Returning from market, Mom looked around. All the work was done. On the hay, the three grown-ups slept soundly. Pipo put a finger to his lips. "Shh."
